about: desktop-design 2.9 (p3_safety.py; the same texts run in src/lib/render/sanitize.test.js): replies that try to run code, load or post to an address, open a link without a click, or look like the app's own permission slot. 127.0.0.1:47321 is p3_safety.py's own listener inside the sandbox: the fake server's port changes every run and a script cannot name it. The only link that may open is the fake page in the links reply. The diagrams reply holds one valid diagram of every kind the renderer supports (render/mermaid.js DIAGRAM_KINDS): each must draw, inline and in the panel.

Only the first one may open: [the fake page](http://127.0.0.1:47321/page.html) [javascript link](javascript:alert(1)) [data link](data:text/html,) [tab first]( javascript:alert(1)) [space first]( javascript:alert(1)) [upper case](JAVASCRIPT:alert(1)) [newline inside](java script:alert(1)) [vbscript link](vbscript:x) [blob link](blob:x) [data html](data:text/html,x) [entity link](javascript:alert(1)) [colon entity](javascript:alert(1)) [reference link][evil] ![bad picture](javascript:alert(1)) raw tab first raw space first raw upper case raw newline inside raw vbscript raw blob raw data [evil]: javascript:alert(1)

A diagram that asks for loose security, HTML labels and click callbacks: ```mermaid %%{init: {"securityLevel": "loose", "htmlLabels": true, "flowchart": {"htmlLabels": true}, "startOnLoad": true}}%% flowchart LR A["Sign in"] --> B[Home] click A call alert("mermaid") click B "javascript:alert(1)" "a link" ``` Math that asks for links and pictures: $\href{javascript:alert(1)}{x}$, $\url{javascript:alert(1)}$ and $\includegraphics{http://127.0.0.1:47321/math.png}$. $$ \href{javascript:alert(1)}{\text{display link}} + \htmlData{onclick=alert(1)}{y} $$
